title: How stalactites and stalagmites grow
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What is the difference between a stalactite and a stalagmite?
How long do stalactites take to grow?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: When they meet, they make a column

explain.say: Water that dripped through limestone carries dissolved calcite. When a drop hangs from a cave ceiling, some carbon dioxide escapes into the cave air, and the water can no longer hold all its calcite.
A tiny ring of calcite is left around each drop. Ring after ring builds a hollow straw that grows into an icicle-shaped stalactite hanging from the roof.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: When they meet, they make a column

explain.say: When the drop falls and splashes on the floor, it leaves a little more calcite there. That builds up into a stalagmite, rising from the ground.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: When they meet, they make a column

explain.say: They grow very slowly, often less than a few millimetres a century to a few millimetres a year. Over thousands of years a stalactite and stalagmite can meet and join into a column.

faq.q: What is the difference between a stalactite and a stalagmite?
faq.a: A stalactite hangs from the cave ceiling and a stalagmite rises from the floor. A trick to remember: stalactites hold tight to the ceiling, and stalagmites might reach up to it one day.
Each drip of water loses a little carbon dioxide to the cave air, which makes it drop some of its dissolved calcite. The calcite builds up ring by ring around the drip, making the stalactite longer.

faq.q: How long do stalactites take to grow?
faq.a: Very slowly, usually from a fraction of a millimetre to a few millimetres a year, depending on how fast water drips and how much calcite it carries. Big ones can be tens of thousands of years old.
asks: How fast does a stalactite grow?

faq.a: A column forms when a stalactite growing down meets a stalagmite growing up, joining into one pillar from floor to ceiling.
asks: What happens when stalactites and stalagmites meet?

faq.a: Best not. Oils from your skin can stop calcite sticking, so the formation stops growing in that spot, and they break easily.
asks: Why can't you touch cave formations?

facts: Stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves are mostly made of calcite, a form of calcium carbonate.
Soda straws are thin, hollow young stalactites the width of a water drop.

quiz.why: Stalagmites build up where drips land on the floor.

wrong.1: Formations hanging from the roof are stalactites.
wrong.2: Formations growing from walls are usually flowstone or helictites, not stalagmites.
